name: M3GNet and MatGL (Materials Graph Library)
subcategory: universal graph interatomic potential and property models
origin_detail: M3GNet by Chen and Ong (Nature Computational Science 2022) in the materialsvirtuallab GitHub org; MatGL, its PyTorch reimplementation, began as 'a collaboration between the Materialyze.AI and Intel Labs' and now sits in the materialyzeai org. University affiliations were not confirmed on fetched pages.

licences.weights: distributed with the repos (no separate licence stated)

openness_notes: Both repos are BSD-3-Clause. M3GNet's universal potential was trained on Materials Project relaxations (MPF.2021.2.8, figshare DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.19470599). The TensorFlow repo was archived on 2025-04-09 ('Users are recommended to use matgl instead'). MatGL v0.1.0 (2023-02-16) reimplemented M3GNet and MEGNet; v3.0.0 (May 2026) dropped the DGL backend for PyTorch Geometric. Microsoft's MatterSim checkpoints are 'based on the M3GNet architecture'. Group I scoring: 0 = no weights; 1 = weights only under non-commercial or gated custom terms; 2 = open code/weights with the flagship model, weights or training data closed (open core); 3 = code and weights under OSI-type or CC BY licences; 4 = 3 plus openly downloadable training data, or outputs published as an open database stewarded by a public institution. Score 4.
risk_events: Framework churn: TensorFlow repo archived (2025), DGL backend dropped (2026)
robustness: BSD code, public training data, and a corporate derivative (MatterSim) that shows the architecture's reuse.
physical_science_relevance: Universal potentials and property prediction across the periodic table; early demonstration that one MLIP can cover 89 elements.

training_data.name: MatPES
training_data.note: Newer MatGL models; details not confirmed on fetched page.

openness_effect_assessment: Permissive licensing let a corporate lab (Microsoft MatterSim) build directly on the architecture, and let an industrial partner (Intel Labs) co-develop the PyTorch port. The cost of openness here is maintenance: two framework migrations in four years.
key_takeaway: Open academic architectures become the substrate for corporate models. Durability depends on continued maintenance more than on the licence.
